title: Policy-driven version promotion with per-tenant health gates for private control planes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build an automation layer and Terraform orchestration that enables policy-driven promotion of control-plane versions in Private (VPC) deployments. The flow must support per-tenant/cluster health gates, progressive traffic promotion, automated rollback, and explicit operator controls.

Why: Current private control-plane upgrades are manual and brittle. We need a repeatable, auditable, and safe promotion path that: (1) reduces human toil for routine upgrades, (2) minimizes blast radius for regressions via tenant-aware canaries, and (3) plugs into existing Private IaC (Terraform) and observability (console/tracing) surfaces.

Scope:
- Terraform modules and community-style examples to provision promotion pipelines and canary slices (no change to public API).
- A policy engine (YAML + CRD) that defines promotion rules: metric thresholds, minimum sample sizes, percentage schedule, and tenant allow/deny lists.
- Health checks: rollout probes (smoke requests), synthetic latency p50/p95, error-rate SLOs, KV cache warmup signals, and warning for backend resource pressure (GPU/IO).
- Automated rollback with reasoned alerts and a manual "promote-now" override for emergencies.
- Audit log entries and GitHub PR automation to create a post-upgrade changelog.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting core control-plane migration logic. This is an orchestration layer that invokes existing upgrade APIs.
- Implementing tenant billing changes as part of promotion.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field)

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: policy engine increases surface area; mitigate by providing sane defaults and simple starter templates.
- False positives on health gates: require sample size and ramp time to avoid flapping.
- Terraform drift: must clearly document required 'force' semantics when operators need immediate promotion versus staged flows.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module: redwood/private-upgrade-pipeline v0.1 with examples for single-tenant and multi-tenant slices.
- Small runtime controller (Go) for executing promotion plan and emitting events to console.
- Runbook and playbook (Markdown) stored in Drive: link in attachments.

Integration points:
- Console: rollout timeline and per-tenant health widgets.
- Alerts: PagerDuty + Slack channel integration for critical rollback events.
- GitHub: PR templates for promotion decisions and automated release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exists with example usage for single-cluster and multi-cluster canaries
Policy YAML can express percentage schedule, min-samples, and tied metrics (latency, error-rate)
Automated promotion can be paused/resumed by an operator with an audit trail
Automatic rollback triggers when any configured gate breaches thresholds for N consecutive evaluation windows
Per-tenant traffic slicing and isolation is honored during promotion (no tenant receives > configured percent before health gates pass)
Console shows timeline, gates, and final promotion decision with links to logs and PRs
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose JSON/YAML-based policy model over a full UI-first workflow to accelerate initial rollout (Maya)
2025-02-18: Use Terraform module authoring pattern instead of bespoke CLI to keep IaC ownership with infra teams (Samuel)
2025-02-24: Gate thresholds will include a min-sample requirement to prevent noisy signals during low-traffic tenants (SRE review)
2025-02-27: Opted to emit events to the Console instead of trying to embed the entire decision UI in the first iteration. Links to traces/logs for deeper inspection.
tasks: Design policy schema and default policies
Build runtime promotion controller (Go) with a small state machine
Add health check probes and integrate with console metrics
Create automated test harness with canary simulation (local & ephemeral clusters)
Create GitHub PR automation to tag promotion decisions and generate release notes

2025-02-13 - Priya Raman (SRE): We should add cache-warmup as a gate — without warm KV caches some tenants show high p95 on first requests. Recommend adding a 'cache-ready' boolean signal from runtime.

2025-02-17 - Samuel Ortiz: Implementing Terraform module skeleton in https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/412 — module exposes 'promotion_policy' as a map and 'canary_slices' as a list.
2025-02-20 - Design review (Lina Park): Console needs an explicit 'why' panel that surfaces which gate failed (latency vs errors vs resource pressure). Added as a UI task.
2025-02-22 - QA (Ethan Jacobs): Wrote canary-sim test harness and observed flapping when sample size < 30; bump default min_samples to 50 in policy defaults.
2025-02-25 - Security (Renee O'Neill): Confirmed no new keys are stored; promotion controller uses existing control-plane upgrade endpoints with current auth. Suggested an audit event schema.
notes: Operator ergonomics are important — provide a "promote-now" override and a 'dry-run' plan. Final UX iteration will be driven by SRE/Infra feedback during alpha tests.
